evidence: test.sh, tests/Dockerfile, environment/Dockerfile and integration.md lines 1-14 are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff empty; task.toml differs only in identity/metadata; integration.md adds lines 15-19). I enumerated every launch assumption in task/tests/test.sh and matched each one to something the agent can read. (1) The entry /app/server.js must exist (test.sh:68) -> instruction.md:13 'start with node /app/server.js'; integration.md:5. (2) Symlinks are rejected unless they resolve inside /app/node_modules (test.sh:72-83) -> integration.md:16-19. (3) The app runs unprivileged as uid 65534 via setpriv (test.sh:110), may run from a writable copy at /tmp/submission (test.sh:90-102), and cwd is not /app (the verifier WORKDIR is /tests, mode go-rwx, tests/Dockerfile:44-45) -> hireops_rules.md:198-201 says 'may launch Node from a working directory other than the application directory. It runs as an unprivileged user and may launch a writable copy... Resolve bundled UI and seed files relative to the entry or module directory'. instruction.md:11 tells the agent to read hireops_rules.md and integration.md. (4) env -i carries only PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT and DB_PATH (test.sh:104-109) -> hireops_rules.md:201-202 lists exactly those five and says 'do not rely on inherited shell variables'; NODE_PATH is in integration.md:3-4; PORT/DB_PATH are in instruction.md:13. (5) PORT=3000 and the probe on 127.0.0.1:3000 (test.sh:48, 108) -> instruction.md:13 'listen on port 3000 (honour PORT if it's set)'; integration.md:5-6 'port 3000 on 0.0.0.0'. All five prompts open http://localhost:3000, consistent with app_context.md:4. (6) DB_PATH=/app/app.db or the copy's app.db (test.sh:98-109) -> instruction.md:13 'keep its durable data in /app/app.db, honouring DB_PATH'. (7) The liveness probe is GET /api/health, then / (test.sh:48; any HTTP response counts) -> instruction.md:13 'expose GET /api/health as a check that never touches the database'; integration.md:9-10. (8) Seed and runtime: /assets is chmod-ed but not relied on (test.sh:88) -> instruction.md:15 'Copy what you need into /app; /assets and /instructions are unavailable at runtime... start with no shipped database'. test.sh does not delete a shipped app.db, and the brief forbids shipping one. (9) Dependencies: the verifier installs express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 globally on node:22 with NODE_PATH (tests/Dockerfile:1-22), the same as the agent image (environment/Dockerfile:1-12) -> integration.md:3-4 'Node 22 ... Express and better-sqlite3 already available through NODE_PATH'; instruction.md:13 'don't install packages'. (10) The restart helper relaunches with the same env and DB (test.sh:127-193) -> instruction.md:15 'keep new work across restarts'; integration.md:8-9. (11) Sign-in, which the gates use: the brief asks for it explicitly (instruction.md:17, accounts and password), so the internal annotation about unrequested login does not apply. Same-origin and network: public by profile, and nothing in the verifier requires same-origin. I tried a plausible conforming alternative that could fail: an app using express.static('public') relative to cwd would break under cwd=/tests as uid 65534. I first suspected an undisclosed assumption, but hireops_rules.md section 8 discloses it explicitly, so the finding is refuted. I tried a plausible broken app that could pass: one that reads /assets/seed_data.json at runtime might still launch, because task.toml artifacts include /assets (template-identical). That is verifier leniency against a stated requirement, not an untold launch assumption, so it is outside this row's failure direction (Note only). The golden matches the contract: bootstrap.js:20 serves /api/health before the DB; bootstrap.js:43 uses PORT || 3000 on 0.0.0.0; db.js:9-10 uses DB_PATH and resolves seed via __dirname; index.js:42 resolves PUBLIC_DIR via __dirname. Runtime evidence: the scripted golden run (workspace.cjs:16) used a sanitized env of PATH/HOME/NODE_PATH/PORT/DB_PATH with cwd /tmp, and its index scope claims uid 65534 plus a real restart. It did NOT execute the actual test.sh, setpriv/env -i or the /tests cwd, and the index scope says the full configured grading run is absent. This row is a source-level contract-agreement check, so that gap belongs to the runtime/launch rows and does not change this verdict. Minor unstated item (Note): test.sh allows about 30 s of readiness polling (test.sh:116-122), and no startup deadline is stated. integration.md:9-10 requires health to answer before DB work, so a conforming app easily meets it.
